review.notes: Complete real v0.4.1 github-auto runtime exports include nine scalar overloads, five logical functions, zero tables and views. All are local read-only tokenization operations; no authentication or write APIs are omitted.

Complete public registration plus the retained release-to-current diff at public main fe84c9fe390dd08ee78d578db1f2506492573d7d establishes the same five functions and nine signatures. All changed worker lines concern example/catalog metadata; the tokenizer engine, adapters, signatures and dependency lock are unchanged. Current mappings are reviewed interface compatibility, not a claim that the notebooks ran current-main code.

review.purpose: Compare exact ordinary-text counts for the same eleven strings under two encodings; distinguish code points, bytes, empty input and unknown metadata.
review.finding: All22 sample/encoding counts match token-ID lengths. o200k has fewer tokens on four strings and equal counts on seven; this is a fixture comparison rather than a language ranking. Empty input returns0 while missing text and unknown encoding remainNULL. The selected-encoding experiment changes ratios without changing the input population or full comparison.

review.purpose: Determine whether equal token counts make token IDs interchangeable across vocabularies.
review.finding: hello world has two tokens in both encodings, but cl100k IDs15339/1917 differ from o200k24912/2375. The encoding belongs with stored IDs; numeric equality or count equality alone cannot identify text across vocabularies.

review.purpose: Resolve stored model labels before measuring one fixed text, preserving unsupported labels.
review.finding: The pinned worker maps gpt-4 tocl100k and gpt-4o too200k; the same Japanese input counts11versus7. unknown-model remainsNULL with no token estimate. Discovery drives the downstream count and is explicitly the release mapping, not current service behavior.

review.purpose: Inspect the text produced when a one-token budget intersects a Unicode character.
review.finding: The ASCII control keeps hello, while the three-token globe emoji yields a replacement character after a one-token cut. One of two controls is lossy, so a valid decoded string is not a lossless prefix of the original bytes. This boundary control remainscl100k in the encoding experiment.

review.purpose: Measure repeated token positions and test whether decoded windows preserve the source token stream.
review.finding: With budget8 and overlap2, the16-token ASCII source produces3windows totaling20tokens; each returnedID slice matches the original and removing overlap reconstructs all16IDs. Zerooverlap gives2windows totaling16tokens. The globe control yieldsthree replacement-character pieces, each individually token5809; concatenation retokenizes to one58432 instead of original9468/234/235. Equal sums of individualwindow counts do not establish lossless reconstruction.
